title: The Anatomy of Tariff Pass-through into Consumer Prices
discussion_signal: The paper author explicitly links NBER Working Paper 35561 and reports that about 26% of the tariff increase passes through to consumer prices. The post separates the direct import-price channel, which accounts for 64% of the estimated pass-through, from the indirect imported-input and domestic-markup channel, which accounts for 36% and takes nine to twelve months to move through supply chains. This makes the industrial-to-household pathway visible rather than treating tariffs as a single border-price effect.
linked_research_question: How do direct import costs, domestic input exposure, market power, inventories, and delayed markup changes distribute tariff burdens across U.S. firms, retailers, and households over time?
limits: The post is a short author summary and does not provide the full product universe or uncertainty estimates
The 26% estimate is relative to less-exposed goods and is not a universal household price effect
A single LinkedIn post is not representative of consumers, firms, retailers, or policymakers
